articles.title: Long-term results of the modified Dunn procedure in slipped capital femoral epiphysis : a minimum of ten-year follow-up.
articles.authors: Aprato A, Audisio A, Grilli S, Giachino M, Reinaudo V, Risitano S, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective single-centre cohort study with long-term follow-up
articles.population: Patients treated with modified Dunn procedure for stable or unstable slipped capital femoral epiphysis of any severity
articles.sample_size: 35 hips in 34 patients with minimum ten-year follow-up
articles.outcomes: Ten-year survival free from hip replacement (88.6%) and from osteoarthritis progression (82.9%); functional scores; hip range of motion; correction of hip deformity angles
articles.take_home: The modified Dunn procedure achieved excellent function and good outcomes at ten years for mild and moderate slips, but osteoarthritis progression was more likely in severe slips. No patients developed avascular necrosis after surgery.

articles.title: The FEAR Framework for Recovery After Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Hershfeld BE, Tauro TM, Klein BJ, Cohn RM, Scuderi GR, Mont MA, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip and knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Persistent pain, functional limitation, dissatisfaction, and recovery after hip and knee replacement surgery
articles.take_home: Fear-related psychological factors, particularly worry about movement and catastrophising about pain, are linked to worse outcomes after hip and knee replacement. A new FEAR Framework (covering fall confidence, avoidance of activity, anxiety, and reinjury fear) may help clinicians identify and address these psychological barriers to recovery.

articles.title: Bleeding and Hemostasis Optimization in Primary and Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Structured Expert-Opinion Survey.
articles.authors: Chen AF, Mont MA, Smitterberg CW, Aflatooni JO, Cohen-Rosenblum AR, Della Valle CJ, et al.
articles.population: Fellowship-trained arthroplasty surgeons with experience in primary and revision total knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Agreement on definition of problematic bleeding, risk factors, escalation triggers, and use of hemostatic agents in knee replacement surgery
articles.take_home: Surgeons agree that problematic bleeding after knee replacement should be defined by clinical events that change treatment (such as significant drop in blood count, ongoing wound drainage, or need for transfusion) rather than just blood loss numbers alone. Topical clotting agents are routinely used in revision surgery but not in routine first-time operations.

articles.title: To Lengthen or Revise: Reevaluating Anterior Acetabular Overhang Thresholds in Iliopsoas Impingement After Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Clark DS, Kelly JJ 4th, Yanamala SR, Helgeson EE, Trousdale RT, Levy BA, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent arthroscopic iliopsoas fractional lengthening following total hip replacement for iliopsoas impingement
articles.outcomes: Visual analogue scale pain scores, modified Harris hip score, Single Assessment Numeric Evaluation score, Tegner activity level, groin pain improvement, hip flexion strength improvement, overall satisfaction, reoperation rates, acetabular revision rates
articles.take_home: Arthroscopic iliopsoas fractional lengthening worked well for patients with iliopsoas impingement after hip replacement, regardless of how much the socket stuck out. This procedure should be considered as a first treatment option even when the socket overhang is large, as it had good results and rarely needed further socket revision surgery.

articles.title: Defining Long-Term Success After Anatomic Total Shoulder Arthroplasty: Survivorship and Clinically Important Outcomes.
articles.authors: Kucharik MP, Hung V, Jones T, Patel R, Ranson WA, Schmidt CM 2nd, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Implant survivorship at 10 and 15 years; American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score; patient satisfaction; revision rates
articles.take_home: Shoulder replacements had excellent implant survival rates (96% at 10 years), and most patients experienced meaningful long-term benefit, though shoulder function gradually declined over time. Younger patients and those with a particular shoulder bone shape (Walch B) had higher risks of needing revision surgery.

articles.title: Cervical Disc Arthroplasty: Evolution, Evidence, and Future Directions in Motion-Preservation Surgery.
articles.authors: Kim MT, Lee S, Goh GS, Riew KD
articles.population: Patients with cervical degenerative disc disease
articles.outcomes: Clinical outcomes, motion preservation, adjacent-segment pathology rates, revision rates
articles.take_home: Cervical disc arthroplasty works as well as spinal fusion surgery for single and double-level neck problems and keeps the spine moving naturally. Although it may reduce problems in the segments next to the surgery compared with fusion, the benefit is modest, and more research with standardised methods is needed.

articles.title: There are No Differences in Early Complications or One-Year Patient-Reported Outcomes Between Single-Stage Bilateral and Unilateral Total Hip Arthroplasty Performed in Patients 70 Years and Older.
articles.authors: Nishi R, Morikawa L, Kim D, Weldon RH, Kaneshiro JM, Nakasone CK
articles.population: Patients aged 70 years and older with hip osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Early postoperative complications within 90 days, length of stay, transfusion rates, emergency department visits, readmissions, venous thromboembolism, reoperations, revisions, and patient-reported outcomes at one year
articles.take_home: Doing hip replacement surgery on both sides in one operation appears safe for people aged 70 and over, with similar complication rates and patient satisfaction compared to operating on just one hip at a time. Patients undergoing bilateral surgery did stay in hospital longer and needed more blood transfusions, but had no more serious complications or emergency visits.

articles.title: Estimating within-patient sagittal pelvic tilt change from routine anteroposterior hip radiographs in patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty : development and temporal validation.
articles.authors: Kobayashi K, Kidera K, Yamada S, Fukushima T, Hozumi A
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 116 patients in derivation cohort; 80 patients in validation cohort
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of estimating pelvic tilt change from standard hip X-rays, compared to CT scan reference standard
articles.take_home: Researchers developed a simple measurement from routine hip X-rays that can accurately estimate how much a patient's pelvis tilts when they move from lying down to standing up. This measurement was accurate to within 3 degrees in over 93% of patients, which should help surgeons better position hip replacements.

articles.title: Ultrasound- and fluoroscopy-guided hip aspiration before revision total hip arthroplasty: procedural outcomes and diagnostic accuracy in sequential cohorts.
articles.authors: Van Schaik TJA, May K, Hannink G, Van Susante JLC, Goosen JHM, Schreuder HWB, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing hip aspiration before revision total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Dry-tap rates, aspirated volumes, complications within 14 days, and diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity and specificity) for detecting periprosthetic joint infection
articles.take_home: Both ultrasound and fluoroscopy guidance had similar rates of failed aspirations (around one-third) and were highly specific for detecting infection, though sensitivity varied between groups. Two minor complications occurred in the ultrasound group, both in patients who also had a biopsy taken.

articles.title: Early Readmission and Mortality Across Periprosthetic Joint Infection Trajectories After Revision Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Yao W, Chen S, Chen X, Yang J, Pei F, Wang D, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision hip or knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: 90-day unplanned readmission after index revision and all-cause mortality
articles.take_home: Patients who developed infection after revision surgery had higher readmission rates within 90 days and increased mortality compared to those without infection. Those whose revision was for infection but then developed infection again had the highest mortality rates.

articles.title: Integrating the Association Research Circulation Osseous Clinical Practice Guideline into the Diagnosis and Management of Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head: Four Illustrative Case Scenarios.
articles.authors: Thomas G, Mirzaei A, Mont MA, Cheng EY
articles.study_type: Clinical practice guideline application with case illustrations
articles.population: Patients with osteonecrosis of the femoral head
articles.outcomes: Appropriate diagnostic imaging, risk stratification, and treatment selection based on ARCO guideline recommendations
articles.take_home: The ARCO clinical practice guideline provides a framework to help doctors decide whether patients with osteonecrosis of the femoral head should be observed, treated with joint-preserving techniques like core decompression, or offered hip replacement, based on factors such as lesion size, age, symptoms, and collapse risk.

articles.title: Cemented Femoral Fixation for Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty in the United States: How Surgeon-Cemented Volume Impacts Failure Risk.
articles.authors: Abrolat JL, Zedan AM, Ahmadi A, Juels M, Taylor JM, Bini S, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national database
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty with cemented femoral fixation, 2016 to 2020
articles.outcomes: All-cause revision, periprosthetic fracture, mechanical loosening, periprosthetic joint infection, and dislocation within five years
articles.take_home: Surgeons who perform fewer than 60 cemented hip replacements over five years have significantly higher revision rates and complications compared to those performing 60 or more. Patients should ensure their surgeon has adequate experience with cemented hip replacements, as the benefits of this technique may be lost if performed by low-volume surgeons.

articles.title: Treatment of Vancouver B2 and B3 Periprosthetic Femoral Fractures Using a Modular Tapered Stem: Survivorship and Radiographic Outcomes at Mean 7.8-Year Follow-Up.
articles.authors: Chaudhry F, Bridger A, Kolhatkar K, Nannapaneni S, Ekhtiari S, Safir OA, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent revision total hip arthroplasty for Vancouver B2 and B3 periprosthetic femoral fractures
articles.outcomes: Survivorship at 15 years was 95.1%. Complication rate was 13.0% (dislocation in 4 patients, infection in 1, iliopsoas tendonitis in 1). Revision rate was 4.3%. At final follow-up, 95.2% of patients were able to walk.
articles.take_home: Revision hip replacement using a modular tapered stem for periprosthetic femoral fractures showed excellent long-term survival with low complication rates at 7.8 years average follow-up. Most patients remained mobile after surgery.

articles.title: Systemic Exposure and Renal Safety After Intrawound Vancomycin Powder in Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Prospective Comparative Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Bingol O, Karlidag T, Ozsoy HE, Aydin T, Keskin OH, Ozkurt B
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Systemic vancomycin absorption, renal function and acute kidney injury, periprosthetic joint infection, superficial infection, and wound complications
articles.take_home: One gram of vancomycin powder placed in the wound during knee replacement surgery was absorbed into the bloodstream only minimally and did not cause kidney damage. However, it did not reduce infection or wound complications compared to surgery without it, so routine use in primary knee replacement cannot be recommended based on these findings.

articles.title: Beyond the Surgical Factors: Preoperative Habits, Cutaneous Sensation, and Adaptive Strategies as Predictors of Kneeling Ability Following Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Juryn MS, Facchinato D, Stoica S, Cecere M, Lex JR, Wolfstadt JI
articles.population: Patients who underwent primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Kneeling ability and frequency after surgery, measured by patient-reported questionnaire assessing preoperative habits, exercise regularity, perceived importance of kneeling, adaptive strategies, and cutaneous patellar sensation
articles.take_home: Patients who exercised regularly before surgery and felt kneeling was important to them were more likely to kneel after their knee replacement. Abnormal skin sensations around the kneecap, particularly burning or shock-like feelings, were associated with reduced kneeling ability.

articles.title: Factors Affecting Changes in Ankle Symptoms Following Total Knee Arthroplasty for Varus Knee Osteoarthritis.
articles.authors: Lee SM, D'Lima D, Yun MS, Kim KB, Woo SH, Suh KT
articles.population: Patients with varus knee osteoarthritis undergoing total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Ankle symptoms measured by Foot Function Index score; radiological parameters including mechanical tibio-femoral angle, talar tilt angle, and hindfoot alignment view angle measured before surgery and at 12 months
articles.take_home: About one in six patients experienced worsening ankle symptoms after knee replacement surgery. Patients with existing ankle arthritis were more likely to have worsening ankle pain, and certain measurements of ankle alignment after surgery were linked to worse ankle symptoms.

articles.title: Impact of Revised Cardiac Risk Index, Individual Risk Factors, and Their Duration on Major Adverse Cardiac Events After Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Nationwide Propensity-Matched Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Chiang LY, Chu YR, Kung PT, Chen CP, Tsai WC
articles.study_type: Retrospective nationwide cohort study with propensity-score matching
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee replacement between 2017 and 2021
articles.outcomes: Major adverse cardiac events at 30 days, 90 days, and 1 year after surgery
articles.take_home: The Revised Cardiac Risk Index reliably predicts heart-related complications after knee replacement, with risk roughly doubling in patients with a score of 2 or more. Patients aged 75 or over with recent kidney problems and a higher risk score need especially close monitoring after surgery.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of Rotating-Hinge Total Knee Arthroplasty in Primary and Revision Settings: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Jabalameli M, Bagherifard A, Askari A, Sour B, Zareie B, Salehpour M
articles.population: Patients undergoing rotating-hinge total knee arthroplasty in primary (first-time) and revision (repeat) settings
articles.sample_size: 110 patients (120 knees): 52 primary knees and 68 revision knees
articles.outcomes: Knee function scores (Knee Society Function Score and Oxford Knee Score), implant survival (re-revision or component exchange), intraoperative fractures, and deep infection rates
articles.take_home: Rotating-hinge knee replacements produced significant improvements in function and patient-reported outcomes in both first-time and revision surgery, with survival rates above 98% at five years. Complications such as fractures and infection occurred but should be considered in the context of the complex knee problems these implants are used to treat.

articles.title: There Were No Differences in Total Knee Arthroplasty Function Following High Tibial Osteotomy or Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty: More Than 10 Years of Follow-Up.
articles.authors: Bax EA, Ahmad RA, Clark SC, van Egmond N, Taunton MJ, Pagnano MW, et al.
articles.study_type: Prospective cohort study with mean 11.5 years follow-up
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee replacement after previous high tibial osteotomy or unicompartmental knee replacement
articles.sample_size: 216 patients (134 after high tibial osteotomy, 82 after unicompartmental knee replacement)
articles.outcomes: Revision rates, infection rates, reoperation rates, Knee Society Scores, and range of motion
articles.take_home: Total knee replacements performed after either high tibial osteotomy or unicompartmental knee replacement had similar revision and infection rates over more than 10 years. Patients who had high tibial osteotomy first showed better functional scores at two and five years, though this difference was small.

articles.title: Closer to Native, Not Clinically Superior: Bi-Unicompartmental versus Total Knee Arthroplasty for Bicompartmental Femoro-Tibial Osteoarthritis, A Randomized Trial.
articles.authors: Sarzaeem MM, Ghanei A, Omrani FA, Kouhsari HJ, Kazemian G, Dolikhani M, et al.
articles.population: Patients with severe bicompartmental knee osteoarthritis, intact cruciate ligaments and minimal kneecap involvement
articles.outcomes: Forgotten Joint Score, Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index, Knee Society Score, Oxford Knee Score, pain score, complications and reoperations at 24 months
articles.take_home: Both types of knee replacement surgery gave similar patient satisfaction and pain relief scores at two years, with no serious complications in either group. Bi-unicompartmental replacement was not better than total knee replacement for carefully selected patients with two-compartment osteoarthritis.

articles.title: Early Recovery Trajectories Identify Patients at Risk for Outcome Deterioration During Postoperative Years One to Five After Medial Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Wang Z, Du M, Cao G, Huang Y
articles.study_type: Prospective cohort study with growth mixture modelling
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Pain (Numerical Rating Scale) and function (Oxford Knee Score) at 1, 3, and 6 months post-operatively, and at 1, 2, and 5 years post-operatively
articles.take_home: Patients who recover slowly from pain and function in the first six months after unicompartmental knee replacement are more likely to develop pain and functional problems over the next five years. Early post-operative monitoring can help identify patients who may need closer follow-up and additional support.

articles.title: Cluster B Personality Disorder Is Independently Associated With Opioid Abuse at Two and Five Years After Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Chebi P, Mzeihem M, Alvarez J, Macgregor K, Rechenmacher A, Mejia A, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national claims database
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty from 2010 to 2022
articles.sample_size: 698,040 patients identified; 2,961 (0.4%) with personality disorder; 2,922 matched pairs analysed
articles.outcomes: Opioid abuse at two and five years post-surgery, wound and infectious complications, medical and orthopaedic complications
articles.take_home: Patients with Cluster B personality disorder were more likely to abuse opioids at two and five years after knee replacement surgery, even though they received similar amounts of opioid painkillers. The study suggests that doctors should screen for personality disorders before surgery and use careful opioid management strategies in these patients.

articles.title: Preoperative varus >/=10 degrees does not compromise outcome after medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty, whereas postoperative joint-line convergence angle and insert thickness influence functional results: A matched-pair analysis.
articles.authors: Weishorn J, Bonnmann S, Trefzer R, Hariri M, Mick P, Lunz A, et al.
articles.population: Patients with anteromedial osteoarthritis undergoing medial mobile-bearing unicompartmental knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Oxford Knee Score, revision rates, implant survival, and postoperative alignment measurements including joint-line convergence angle and insert thickness
articles.take_home: Patients with significant knock-knee deformity (10 degrees or more) can have medial knee replacement with outcomes as good as those with less deformity, provided the surgeon achieves the correct post-operative alignment and avoids using implants that are too thick. The positioning of the joint line after surgery and implant thickness were the main factors affecting how well patients did.

articles.title: Developing a new CT-based bone defect classification in revision knee arthroplasty : a Delphi consensus study.
articles.authors: de Bondt MR, van Laarhoven SN, van Hellemondt GG, Porteous A, Tuijthof GJM, Heesterbeek PJC, et al.
articles.population: International knee revision surgery experts
articles.sample_size: 56 experts in round one, 37 in round two
articles.outcomes: Consensus on principles for developing a CT-based bone defect classification for revision knee replacement surgery
articles.take_home: Experts agreed that CT imaging should be used to classify bone defects in revision knee replacements and that this should help guide surgical planning and choice of implant. However, they could not agree on the exact anatomical landmarks that should define different zones of the knee bone.

articles.title: Persistent alterations in muscle activation patterns during landing tasks after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction in return-to-sport cohorts: A systematic review and meta-analysis of electromyography studies.
articles.authors: Han Y, Chen Y, Wang Z, Wang TYF, Zhang Y, Sun Y, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis of electromyography studies
articles.population: People who had anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction and returned to sport, compared with healthy controls
articles.sample_size: 556 individuals with ACLR and 501 healthy controls across 32 studies
articles.outcomes: Muscle activation patterns during landing tasks measured by electromyography, including medial hamstrings, gluteus maximus and rectus femoris activation
articles.take_home: People who have had ACL reconstruction and returned to sport show some differences in how their leg muscles activate during landing compared to healthy people, particularly in single-leg tasks. However, it is unclear whether these differences matter clinically and more research is needed to understand their significance.

articles.title: When legal reasoning contradicts sports orthopaedic evidence.
articles.authors: Kennedy JG, Adams S, Batista J, Bayer S, Clanton T, D'Hooghe P, et al.
articles.population: Professional athletes with ankle fractures and concomitant intra-articular pathology
articles.outcomes: Comparison of legal ruling conclusions with current scientific evidence regarding arthroscopy during ankle fracture fixation and risk of posttraumatic arthritis
articles.take_home: The authors argue that a court ruling incorrectly blamed arthroscopic surgery for ankle arthritis in a footballer, when evidence shows posttraumatic arthritis commonly follows ankle fractures regardless of arthroscopy, and arthroscopy is standard care for managing intra-articular damage at the time of fracture fixation.

articles.title: Development and validation of a deep learning-based automated Notch Width Index measurement system from anteroposterior knee radiographs.
articles.authors: Tian J, Saito A, Iriuchishima T, Lee SY, Kato T
articles.study_type: Development and validation of an automated measurement system
articles.population: Knee radiographs from public datasets and external sources
articles.sample_size: 33 radiographs for main validation; 500 external radiographs for feasibility testing
articles.outcomes: Notch Width Index measurement agreement between automated system and manual surgeon measurements; reproducibility; processing speed; segmentation accuracy
articles.take_home: A computer system can measure the Notch Width Index from knee X-rays much faster and more consistently than doctors measuring by hand, though it works less well on poor-quality or arthritic images. The automated method could help standardise measurements for ACL injury risk assessment.

articles.title: Meniscal Root Tears: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Management, and Outcomes.
articles.authors: Livingston M, Ross P, Saraf SM, Christiansen M, Miller JR, Mulcahey MK
articles.population: Patients with meniscal root tears
articles.outcomes: Diagnosis methods, management approaches, and long-term outcomes including osteoarthritis progression and functional recovery
articles.take_home: Root repair gives better long-term results than partial meniscectomy or no surgery in suitable patients, though there is no standard recovery protocol yet. Most approaches restrict weight-bearing and deep squatting for 4 to 5 months after repair.

articles.title: The rate of total hip arthroplasty after closed reduction of late-detected hip dislocation : 147 hips followed to patient age 70 years.
articles.authors: Terjesen T, Wensaas A
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with long-term follow-up
articles.population: Patients diagnosed with late-detected developmental dysplasia and dislocation of the hip before age three years, treated with closed reduction alone
articles.outcomes: Rate of total hip replacement by patient age 70 years; risk factors for hip replacement; survival rates based on residual acetabular dysplasia status
articles.take_home: Hip replacements were eventually needed in 35% of patients by an average age of 53 years. Those without remaining hip socket problems at skeletal maturity had good long-term outcomes, with only 24% needing replacement by age 70, but those with remaining problems had much worse outcomes, with 59% needing replacement by age 70.

articles.title: In vivo 3D hip kinematics during racket swinging after total hip arthroplasty : evaluation of dynamic range of motion and liner-to-neck contact.
articles.authors: Nakao Y, Hamai S, Murakami K, Harada S, Kawahara S, Ikebe S, et al.
articles.population: Patients playing racket sports after primary total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: 3D dynamic hip kinematics during racket swinging, liner-to-neck contact occurrence, posterior clearance measurements, factors associated with reduced clearance
articles.take_home: Racket swinging after hip replacement is generally safe, with liner-to-neck contact occurring in only 8% of cases. The risk of contact can be reduced by careful choice of hip implant design and positioning at the time of surgery.

articles.title: Indications for revision following Birmingham Hip Resurfacing : insights from the largest 25-year series from a design centre.
articles.authors: Nasser AAHH, Samra I, Treacy RBC, Hussain S
articles.population: Patients who underwent Birmingham Hip Resurfacing between July 1997 and July 2022
articles.sample_size: 4,513 BHR cases, of which 392 (8.7%) were revised
articles.outcomes: Revision rates by sex, age and implant head size; indications for revision including aseptic loosening, adverse reaction to metal debris (ARMD), and periprosthetic fractures; implant survival analysis
articles.take_home: Male patients had much lower revision rates (4.7%) than female patients (17.8%), and larger implant sizes (50 mm or more) had better survival than smaller ones. The most common reasons for needing a second operation were loosening of the implant and reactions to metal debris, with metal reactions occurring much later than fractures.

articles.title: Validation of the European Bone & Joint Infection Society recommendations for debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention in hip and knee periprosthetic joint infection : a study from specialist and non-specialist hospitals in the UK.
articles.authors: Hotchen AJ, Richards J, Thumbadoo RP, Tan SJH, Foster P, Canbilen SW, et al.
articles.study_type: Multicentre retrospective cohort study validating clinical recommendations
articles.population: Adults with hip or knee periprosthetic joint infection treated with debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention across seven UK hospitals
articles.outcomes: Treatment failure (need for further surgery, long-term antibiotics, death within 90 days, amputation, or arthrodesis) over median 2.1 years follow-up
articles.take_home: Following European guidelines for selecting patients and exchanging implant components during treatment of infected hip and knee replacements improved success rates to around 79 per cent in the best cases, compared with 28 per cent when guidelines suggested DAIR was not recommended and components were not exchanged. Exchanging components was strongly associated with better outcomes.

articles.title: New guidelines for the prevention of periprosthetic joint infection : a ten-year update.
articles.authors: Ferrini A, He M, Papalia R, He W, Gehrke T, Parvizi J
articles.population: Patients undergoing arthroplasty (joint replacement)
articles.outcomes: Prevention strategies for periprosthetic joint infection
articles.take_home: This updated guidelines review summarises the latest evidence on how to prevent serious infections after joint replacement surgery, though high-quality evidence remains limited in many areas.

articles.title: Diaphyseal zonal fixation in revision total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Sculco PK, El-Hassan M, Shichman I, Lee E, Morgan-Jones R, Haddad FS
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision total knee arthroplasty or distal femoral replacement
articles.outcomes: Implant survivorship and durable fixation in the diaphyseal bone zones
articles.take_home: The authors describe a new classification system dividing the thighbone shaft into three zones to help surgeons plan and achieve better fixation during complex knee replacement revision surgery. This approach may improve outcomes for patients needing multiple revision operations or distal femoral replacements.

articles.title: Ten-year insert wear and the migration of uncemented tibial and femoral components with either conventional polyethylene or sequentially annealed highly crosslinked polyethylene: a blinded randomized controlled trial using radiostereometric analysis.
articles.authors: de Ridder R, Kaptein BL, Pijls BG, Nelissen RGHH, Pasma JH, Oomen R, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing uncemented total knee replacement with fixed insert cruciate-retaining prosthesis
articles.outcomes: Insert wear measured by radiostereometric analysis, tibial and femoral component migration, patient-reported outcome measures at ten years
articles.take_home: Highly crosslinked polyethylene inserts showed no additional wear progression after five years, whilst conventional polyethylene inserts continued to wear. Both types of insert remained stable in the knee replacement at ten years, suggesting highly crosslinked polyethylene is safe to use.

articles.title: Evaluation of the clicky hip as a screening tool in the diagnosis of developmental dysplasia of the hip.
articles.authors: Poacher AT, Bilal M, Smith A, Scourfield L, Hawes E, Ross M, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected registry data
articles.population: Live births in a UK tertiary centre catchment area, January 2016 to December 2023
articles.outcomes: Pathological developmental dysplasia of the hip requiring treatment; positive predictive value of clicky hip finding
articles.take_home: A clicky hip detected at birth or at six to eight weeks was independently linked to developmental dysplasia of the hip requiring treatment, with about one in 26 screened infants with a clicky hip having the condition. The findings support referring babies with a documented clicky hip for ultrasound screening in the UK selective screening pathway.

articles.title: The impact of changing Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee classification on early functional outcomes after primary robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Zaidi F, Goplen CM, Akbarshahi M, MacDessi SJ, Petterwood J, McEwen P, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Oxford Knee Scores at three months, six months and one year postoperatively; changes in Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee classification; lateral distal femoral angle and medial proximal tibial angle measurements
articles.take_home: Most patients had some change in knee alignment after robotic-assisted knee replacement, but those whose alignment shifted by two categories showed smaller improvements in function scores at three and six months. Changing the femoral (thighbone) alignment by more than 4 degrees appeared to cause more functional problems than similar changes to the tibia (shinbone).

articles.title: Higher femoral periprosthetic fracture rate with dual-mobility compared with single-mobility total hip arthroplasty : a retrospective propensity-matched study of 780 uncemented hips.
articles.authors: Komat M, Sabot L, Simion F, Lechien D, Bhogal H, Gan El E, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing uncemented total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Periprosthetic fracture rate, dislocation rate, and mortality
articles.take_home: Dual-mobility hip implants reduce the risk of dislocation but may increase the risk of fractures around the implant compared with standard implants. The choice between these implant types involves trading off protection against dislocation for a potentially higher fracture risk.
